title: Using variables and placeholders to reuse the same prompt

videos.script: A prompt with holes in it is a template, and every prompt in this course has been one. {{title}} The reply prompt has three holes: the shop, the language and the customer's message. Change one value and the same file answers in Portuguese. {{holes}} Leave one empty and the harness refuses to render it. Many template engines would fill the hole with nothing and carry on, and nobody would notice. {{missing}} Pass a value the template never uses, and you get a warning. Somebody believes they are setting the tone, and nothing reaches the model. {{unused}} Then a customer types the tag that closes their own message. The text after it falls outside, where it reads like an instruction. One filter on the value puts it back inside. {{escape}} And the model obeys the instruction anyway. Escaping fixes the shape of the prompt; it does not decide what the model does with the words. {{obeys}} Last comes the prompt id. It is a hash of the file. Change a setting on the command line and the id stays the same, which is why the settings belong in the file. {{close}}
